title: Owner-occupied real estate financing
metaDescription: Owner-occupied real estate projects usually start with SBA 504 and SBA 7(a) comparisons. Learn which fixed-asset routes commonly fit a purchase, build, or refinance plan.
summary: The owner-occupied real-estate use-case page compares the financing routes most often evaluated when the goal is buying, building, improving, or refinancing property used by the business.

hero.title: Financing owner-occupied property starts with the fixed-asset routes.
hero.lead: Property purchases, build-outs, and refinance projects usually call for a different comparison set than working-capital or acquisition requests. This page brings those real-estate paths into one place.

quickAnswer.definition: usually begins with SBA 504 and SBA 7(a) comparisons because those routes commonly cover property projects used directly by the business, while working-capital products are generally meant for different needs.

whoItFits.heading: When owner-occupied real-estate financing tends to fit
items: Buying commercial property that the business will occupy
Building out, renovating, or improving a facility tied directly to operations
Comparing fixed-asset routes before choosing between SBA 504 and a more flexible SBA structure
Projects where property details, occupancy plan, and business financials can already be documented

whenItMayNotFit.heading: When this path may not fit as well
items: If the business really needs inventory or day-to-day operating cash, working-capital products are usually the better first comparison.
If there is no qualifying owner-occupied project, a more flexible route may fit better than a fixed-asset structure.

commonQuestions.question: What routes are usually compared for owner-occupied real estate?
commonQuestions.answer: Borrowers commonly start with SBA 504 and SBA 7(a) because both can play a role in property projects, though 504 is built more specifically for qualifying long-term fixed assets.

commonQuestions.question: Why is SBA 504 often part of the conversation?
commonQuestions.answer: SBA 504 is designed for owner-occupied commercial real estate and major equipment, which makes it a common fixed-asset comparison point for property projects.

commonQuestions.question: What documents usually matter for an owner-occupied property request?
commonQuestions.answer: Common examples include project or property details, business financial statements, cash-flow support, and ownership or occupancy information. Exact requirements vary by lender, CDC, and project.

commonQuestions.question: Does Fund44 provide the property financing directly?
commonQuestions.answer: No. Fund44 does not provide property financing directly. Lenders, CDCs, and SBA program rules determine the final structure and terms.
